findings.evidence: official-replica-label-and-source asserts the quoted label "bigbank-api*** x8" and the Simon Brown dozen-boxes sentence with their URLs; render-with-installed-mmdc asserts which mmdc command and version wording the answer uses
findings.fix: Keep the behavior evals (repo-evidence, render-fix, element fields, boundaries). Replace these two with prompts that produce a diagram and assert the diagram: replicas written in one node label, and a view over 20 elements split by bounded context. Leave the source URLs in the reference files.

findings.evidence: The same two evals test reciting a reference quote and a command sentence rather than producing architecture documentation, which is the skill's stated purpose
findings.fix: Tie the evals to the purpose by asserting the generated diagram, or remove them and add a drop row for each in docs/audit/recovery/c4-architecture/record.md. Do not remove the credit lines or the sourced quotes from the reference files.

findings.evidence: Rel(customer, spa, "Uses", "HTTPS") and Rel(signIn, security, "Validates with") are the rendered examples, while SKILL.md step 5 and common-mistakes.md Generic relationship labels forbid a single word such as "Uses"
findings.fix: Replace those labels with a verb plus what is sent, for example "Views balances" and "Validates credentials with", and give each Rel a technology, so the syntax examples pass the step 5 check they are the fallback for.

findings.evidence: Produce a Component view when the user asks, or when one container holds distinct responsibilities (about five or more modules is a hint, never a gate)
findings.fix: Keep the user-ask and the offer as the defaults. Add one line: when the user named no container and did not ask, write Context and Container and stop; do not also write the Component file in the same run.

findings.evidence: Step 2(b) Split, step 3 Close by purpose, and step 5's What-Why-How labels restate the same purpose rules already given in step 2(c); the restated lines are activation or generic drafting knowledge, so expert content is under 70% of the 52-line body.
findings.fix: Keep the purpose list once in step 2 and point steps 3 and 5 at it. Move the reusable subject-tag and body-structure rules, which users ask for by name, into a skill bundled by the command-compose-email plugin and load that file only when drafting the subject or body; record the move in docs/audit/recovery/compose-email/record.md.

findings.evidence: The command follows a Process pattern (ordered workflow, checkpoints, medium freedom) but the phases are one dense paragraph each with no checkpoint between strategy and close, so the pattern is clear with a minor deviation.
findings.fix: Keep the five steps and add a one-line checkpoint after step 2: purpose chosen, blocking gaps closed, split decided, before step 3 closes the draft.

findings.evidence: Most Gotchas give a non-obvious why (proposed dates read as commitments; unflagged placeholders get pasted and sent; suspected causes become facts), but 'NEVER put the ask only in the subject line' only restates that mobile clients truncate subjects.
findings.fix: Replace that item with a reason an expert learned the hard way, for example that a subject-only ask is dropped when the thread is forwarded without the subject, or drop the item and record the removal in docs/audit/recovery/compose-email/record.md.

findings.evidence: description: Draft or rewrite a professional email to a peer, stakeholder, manager or leadership using What-Why-How. Use for status updates, approval requests, escalations, follow-ups, or when the user only asks to make a message shorter, clearer or less defensive, even without the word email. Produces a subject and body to paste; never sends. Not for casual chat replies; a finished draft can be reformatted for Slack or Teams on request.
findings.fix: Draft or rewrite a professional email (subject plus body) with What-Why-How for a status update, approval request, escalation, follow-up or FYI. Use when the user asks to email a peer, stakeholder, manager or leadership, or only to make a message shorter, clearer or less defensive, even without the word email. Not for casual chat replies and not for sending mail (paste-only; Slack or Teams reformatting is on request).

findings.evidence: Step 2(c) lists six purposes with no default and no order for overlap: a status update that needs a decision is a request, an escalation can also be a follow-up, and 'anything else' is FYI, so two purposes can both match.
findings.fix: Default to one purpose and name the escape: if the reader must decide or approve, it is a Request even when it also reports status or follows up; use Escalation only when impact, uncertainty and a mitigation are all present; otherwise FYI.

findings.evidence: Five scenarios have verifiable assertions, but every prompt says 'You cannot run commands or ask questions' and 'never reply that information is missing', so the blocking-gap path (step 1: no topic and no source draft, ask once and stop) is never actually exercised; empty-request-asks-for-facts contradicts the command it tests.
findings.fix: Add a failure-path scenario whose prompt allows the one blocking question and forbids inventing an email, with assertions that the output asks for topic, recipient and outcome and then stops, and drop the 'never reply that information is missing' line from that scenario only.

findings.evidence: Example Usage is only `/command-compose-email:compose-email <context or pasted draft>` and never shows a finished subject or body, so the example does not reach an output.
findings.fix: Under Example Usage, add one short input (a deadline-extension request) and the subject-plus-body the workflow produces, including a labelled proposed date and the placeholder list.

findings.evidence: Step 2(c) has no resolved branch when a message is both an escalation and a follow-up (prior thread plus observed impact and uncertainty): either purpose can be chosen and the closing rule in step 3 then differs.
findings.fix: Add one tie-break: if a prior unanswered ask exists, Follow-up wins and the escalation content (impact, uncertainty, mitigation) goes in Why; otherwise Escalation.

findings.evidence: Step 4's word-limit fallback says to ask whether to relax the limit or drop named items and then redraft, but it does not say what to do when the user does not answer or names nothing to drop.
findings.fix: State the fallback: if the user does not choose, keep every source fact, leave the overage reported, and do not drop items.

findings.evidence: The command is 468 lines, and phase 5 still inlines the new-PR and existing-PR gh pr create/edit --attach forms, the no-PNG form, and the no-URL failure path, even though 'Branch publish and attach recovery' is already split into skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md.
findings.fix: Move the remaining phase 5 gh create/edit command forms and the no-URL failure path into the 'Branch publish and attach recovery' section of skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md, and leave phase 5 as the condition that loads that section.

findings.evidence: Phase 5 repeats the gh pr create and gh pr edit --attach invocations, the title-file rule, and the no-PNG rule that phase 2, section 5 and the loaded pr-body.md already state.
findings.fix: Keep one canonical copy of those invocations in skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md and point phase 5 at it; do not delete the recovery outcomes.

findings.evidence: 2.2 says the promotion history must show merge commits and that every SRC entry is a PR merged into the current head, but gives no outcome when git log --merges lists some of the source merges and omits others.
findings.fix: State that a partial merge-commit list is the same stop: do not publish, and ask for --reuse-from=<PR>.

findings.evidence: Phase 4 treats empty output, any other output, or a non-zero exit of 'bash "$PRD" capability' as branch mode, while skills/pr-diagrams/scripts/pr-diagrams.sh documents capability as printing attach or branch and always exiting 0; a usage error exits 2 with empty stdout.
findings.fix: Say that exit 2 (or any non-zero exit with empty stdout) is the branch fallback, and that a non-empty stdout other than exactly 'attach' is branch mode, matching the script's exit line.

findings.evidence: The description names open, write, refresh, describe, explain PR changes, promotion and reuse, but not the accepted argument tokens --diagrams, --reuse-from and --base.
findings.fix: Create or update the GitHub pull request for the current branch from its committed diff: summary, changeset triage, optional Mermaid or draw.io diagram, promotion-branch bodies reused from merged PRs, and reviewers. Use when asked to open, write, refresh or describe a pull request, "explain PR changes", "open or refresh the PR summary", "promote develop to main", or "reuse merged PR bodies", including with --diagrams=none|mermaid|drawio, --reuse-from=<PR>, or --base=<branch>. Pushes feature branches and writes PRs. Not for a read-only explanation of a diff (use explain-changes-mental-model).

findings.evidence: The Gotchas list states the jq -j, squash-merge and screenshot facts, but not why a body without a trailing newline glues the next heading, or why an older cycle is selected.
findings.fix: Add the reason to those two Gotchas: jq -j omits the newline so the next printf heading joins the last line, and a squash or rebase leaves the older cycle's commits inside origin/$base..origin/$head.

findings.evidence: 1.1 says to add 'Close <remaining arguments>' joined, while phase 3b says to add that line to the summary, without saying whether it is its own line or part of the 150-word paragraph.
findings.fix: Pick one default in both places: a separate final line 'Close <remaining arguments joined by spaces>', not counted against the 150-word summary.
